first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent it, so I read it properly, top to bottom on the iPad. Place cards are her department, not mine, but the opening is plain and sensible and it promises the practical bits (seating plan, reading them after dark, overseas). That's what kept me going. No silly slang, short paragraphs, I could follow it.

journey.quote: Take every name from one source, your finished seating plan, and check spelling, titles and preferred names before anything is made.
journey.reaction: Good. Aunt Joan will notice if she's 'Mrs' when she should be 'Dr'. Sensible advice and it's up front.

journey.quote: Give your caterer the list of what is in each edible card and of guests with allergies.
journey.reaction: I was glad to see this. My grandson has a nut allergy and I'd have been the one asking. They've thought about it properly, and they say it's general information, not legal advice, which I respect.

journey.quote: Test a sample by candlelight: if it isn't legible at a glance, choose a bolder ink or a plainer script.
journey.reaction: Yes. My mother is 88 and won't read fancy gold script on a mirror in the dark. I'd have liked it to say outright that older guests need the name big enough to read, but this is close.

journey.section: Glass, Mirror and Acrylic Place Cards
journey.quote: Clear acrylic disappears against white linen, so a tinted or frosted finish, or a contrasting lettering colour, keeps the name readable.
journey.reaction: Practical. They're not just selling pretty pictures, they tell you where it goes wrong.

journey.section: Place Cards for a Destination Wedding
journey.quote: Who sets them out? Someone needs the plan, the cards and time before guests arrive. Agree whether that is the venue, your planner or your stylist.
journey.reaction: This is the question I'd ask. Who is actually responsible on the day? I'd want that agreed in writing, not just agreed over a chat with the venue.

journey.section: Place Cards for a Destination Wedding
journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for the venue, travel, vendors and payments, and works in your time zone.
journey.reaction: Now this is the bit for me. One person, and in our time zone, so I'm not ringing Italy at 2am. And payments are included. I'd want to know who that person is and whether I can speak to them on the phone.

journey.quote: Send each stationer your chosen idea, the setting and the final name list from your seating plan, and ask to see a sample.
journey.reaction: Fine, but nothing about getting a written quote or what the deposit is. If my daughter is paying a stationer she's found in a directory, I'd want the price and deposit terms on paper before she pays anything.

journey.section: Plan the table with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD and agrees the fee with you in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: That's exactly what I want to hear. Australian dollars and the fee in writing first. This line makes me willing to forward it to Geoff.

unanswered_questions: Can I speak to the Wedded Advisor on the phone before anything is booked, or is it all done online?
Who is the actual person, and do they stay with us for the whole wedding?
If we pay a stationer through Wedded Marketplace, are deposits protected in any way, or is that between us and the stationer?
If an Advisor manages payments to overseas vendors, how are deposits held and in what currency?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the day overseas?

turn_offs_found.quote: Find a stationer on Wedded Marketplace, our directory of venues and vendors, and compare styles.
turn_offs_found.why: It sends us off to pay a supplier but says nothing about contracts, deposits or getting the quote in writing. That's my exact worry with suppliers, particularly overseas.

would_share_with: My husband Geoff, with the Wedded Advisor paragraph highlighted and the question 'can we ring them?'
My daughter, to say the allergy part and the candlelight test are worth doing

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD and agrees the fee with you in writing before any work begins. Start a conversation through Wedded Concierge
cta_reaction.why: Not about place cards. But the AUD quotes, fee in writing and one person in our time zone are what I look for. I'd click to see whether I can book a phone call. If it's only a chat box or a form, I'd leave it to my daughter.

top_3_changes: Where to Find a Stationer: old "Send each stationer your chosen idea, the setting and the final name list from your seating plan, and ask to see a sample." new "Send each stationer your chosen idea, the setting and the final name list from your seating plan, and ask to see a sample and a written quote that sets out the deposit and delivery date." (Reader-side advice only; names no vendor and makes no claim about how the brand sources, vets or protects suppliers.)

Legibility in evening light: old "For place cards, that means a name in strong contrast, the same position on every setting, and little else on the card." new "For place cards, that means a name in strong contrast and large enough for older relatives to read, the same position on every setting, and little else on the card."
Place Cards for a Destination Wedding: old "Agree whether that is the venue, your planner or your stylist." new "Agree in writing whether that is the venue, your planner or your stylist."
